reference.source: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine / standard rheumatology references
clinicalPearls: An acronym for synovitis, acne, pustulosis, hyperostosis, and osteitis, describing a syndrome linking chronic sterile bone and joint inflammation with characteristic skin disease
The anterior chest wall (sternoclavicular and manubriosternal region) is the most commonly and characteristically affected skeletal site
Palmoplantar pustulosis and severe (including fulminant) acne are the typical associated dermatoses
Bone lesions represent sterile osteitis with reactive hyperostosis rather than infection
It is regarded as belonging within the spondyloarthritis and autoinflammatory spectrum, and some patients are HLA-B27 positive
Bone scintigraphy classically shows increased uptake in the anterior chest wall producing a bull's head sign
Treatment draws on NSAIDs, bisphosphonates, conventional disease-modifying agents, and TNF inhibitors, with the aim of controlling pain and inflammation
Chronic recurrent multifocal osteomyelitis is considered the paediatric counterpart of the same disease spectrum
reference.pathophysiology: SAPHO is a chronic autoinflammatory disorder in which dysregulated innate immunity produces sterile neutrophilic inflammation of bone (osteitis) with secondary reactive new bone formation (hyperostosis), together with neutrophilic skin disease such as palmoplantar pustulosis. Proinflammatory cytokines including TNF and IL-1 are implicated, and there is overlap with the seronegative spondyloarthropathies.
additionalInvestigations: Bone scintigraphy for the characteristic anterior chest wall uptake pattern
MRI of affected skeletal sites to demonstrate osteitis and marrow oedema
Bone biopsy when needed to exclude infection or malignancy, showing sterile inflammation
Dermatological assessment of pustular or acneiform skin lesions
redFlags: Clinical or imaging features that cannot confidently be distinguished from infective osteomyelitis without biopsy
Rapidly destructive or atypical bone lesions raising concern for malignancy
Severe unremitting anterior chest wall pain limiting function
reference.prognosis: The course is typically chronic and relapsing but rarely life-threatening; symptoms often wax and wane and can usually be controlled with anti-inflammatory and immunomodulatory therapy, though some patients have persistent pain and skeletal deformity.
pitfalls: Misinterpreting sterile osteitis as bacterial osteomyelitis and giving prolonged antibiotics
Overlooking the diagnostic link between the skin disease and the bone lesions
Failing to image the anterior chest wall, the most characteristic site
Mistaking hyperostotic bone lesions for malignancy
